title: Yardley public library

paragraphs.text: You will hear a radio program describing the services available at a local library.
First, you have some time to look at questions eleven to fourteen.
Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to fourteen.
Welcome to Community Corner. This week, I'll tell you about services at the Yardley Public Library.

If you're looking for a really quiet place to read or do schoolwork, a study room is best. This is also good for small group study, so you can discuss and learn together. Room sizes vary and can hold from three to seven people. Bookings are done online, but keep in mind that a library card is required to do this. You're limited to two bookings a week. If you're running late, don't worry. You can still have your study room even if you show up ten minutes late. Once you're there, you may ask the librarian to keep the room longer. If there's no booking after you, you may stay.

Meeting rooms at the library are available for large groups of people. Types of events that are usually held in meeting rooms include community meetings and small conferences. These rooms are available at a cost, and payment is made ahead of time. But the cost of a room booking depends on how large the room is. Now, one advantage of these rooms is they can be booked for times when the library's closed. For example, you can book them from nine to eleven at night. And one of these rooms is next to a kitchen, but access to the kitchen must be arranged in advance. For an additional charge, you can use a projector or a laptop for presentations. It should be noted individuals under eighteen can use the meeting room as long as the adult who made the booking is present.
Before you hear the rest of the program, you have some time to look at questions fifteen to twenty.
Now listen and answer questions fifteen to twenty.
Now, I'd like to tell you about some interesting programs for adults at the Yardley Public Library.

Our program, Tech Play, gives adults a chance to build and work with robots. You're shown how it's done first, then you get to make one of your own. You don't have to be a tech genius to have fun with these amazing little playthings.

Power Up helps you learn the basics of how to create and set up your own video game on the computer. It's lots of fun. Different programs will be available, and you'll get to create a game of your own. You don't need to be a computer whiz to do this.

Creativity Club gives you a chance to work with your hands. This is a fun night of relaxation with friends. We'll provide several ideas for things to make and do each week and ask participants to try one they've never done before and to work in small groups to complete the task. You'll be amazed by what you can produce together.

At Brain Break, you can take some time away from the office and de-stress. Have fun putting together your own pictures from discarded library magazines and books. Cut out pictures and paste them on paper in new designs. Put up your creation in the library display case or take it home.

Join the library for Social Paint Night. No need to bring anything. Paints, brushes, and canvases are provided. You'll also get a detailed manual with easy instructions on how to paint a famous landscape step by step. Follow along and make one of your own. Light refreshments are provided.

On Thursday evening, we have the Knitter's Corner. We've a lot of younger people who want to learn how to knit sweaters and blankets. There are always two people here who've been doing this for years to help you. We've a flexible format. Join in when you can and leave when you want to. Thanks for listening, everyone. Join us next week when we'll tell you about the city zoo.
That is the end of part two. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to part two.
